# Chapter 1: Day one.

Yesterday was really stressful.

All in a single day, we got our mission, ran around a space station, found our captain dead, fought our way through a group of hostiles, and almost got killed afterward. I didn’t think this mission was going to be so demanding.

Well, it’s nothing I can’t handle. But the others seem pretty shaken up. Dutch fared the worst out of all of us. One of those demons in armor crushed his entire side. I heard the crunch.

I hope we don’t have to run into that group again.

At least our current destination isn’t so bad. Hypernet search says it’s entirely covered in ocean, which either means this will be easy or depressingly boring. Then again, surely we can all keep each other entertained.

I didn’t sleep much last night. There’s a lot running through my head at the moment. I’m worried that the Republic—

“[Zion, d’we got any snacks around? Or some water? I’m feelin’ real peckish right ab’t now]{Dutch Elkins},” Dutch inquired. It was nearing noontime, and no one was really doing much around the ship.

“[Dutch, why are you up? I thought Bellow told you to stay downstairs and rest]{Zion Daybreaker},” Zion chided. The last thing this crew needed right now was someone incapacitated. Especially not when danger—or riches, potentially—could appear at any moment.

“[Ain’t no one gunna tell me what ta do! Hell, m’ side feels better ‘lready. Bellow bandag’d me up real good, ‘n even got me sum crutches!]{Dutch Elkins}” exclaimed Dutch, happily waving a crutch in the air.

“[Well, there may be some groceries left in the kitchen. And there’s plenty of GUice. Help yourself]{Zion Daybreaker},” Zion answered.

“[Goo-ice!? You try’na poison me!? I’m hurt enough as’t is… you got some nerve!]{Dutch Elkins}” hollered the angry Verinian.

“[Just drink it.]{Zion Daybreaker}”

# Chapter 2: Day two.

I think the monotony is starting to sink in.

We were hopeful yesterday that the sonar would pick something up, or at the very least that we’d encounter something. But it’s just been nothing. No alert, no land, no other ships. We can see some shallow marine life, but that’s about it.

The morning report from the Llamanian Republic was depressing. Not only did I have to admit we hadn’t found anything, but the commander sounded especially annoyed when we told him how we were sailing. Well, I hardly think that’s our fault. The ship can float—what were we expected to do? Pull a canoe out of thin air?

At the very least, things inside the ship seem to be going well. Dutch’s injuries are healing considerably faster than I’d expected. It seems like Bellow knows what he’s doing.

Morra, however… it’s been a bit of a struggle. I’m having trouble connecting with them, or just understanding them in general. Every time I start to ask them something, or just give a report, they start trailing off on the most mundane, unrelated subject. I do NOT CARE about the caste system on Silvangia. I do NOT NEED to know about the cause and result of the Floran Scattering. I just want to do our job.

“[Ah! Hello, Zion. Apologies for the sudden entrance, but I must ask you something—is your metal exterior part of your body?]{Morra}” asked Morra, very curiously. Indeed, Zion had been rather secretive about his nature and past, which was beginning to frustrate Morra. The golem was not, however, the only frustrated one.

“[Morra, do—]{Zion Daybreaker}” Zion sighed, restraining his annoyance. “[Yes, it is technically part of me. Though I prefer to call it my armor]{Zion Daybreaker},” explained the Angelic crewmate.

“[If I may ask, in that case, is it not more similar to a shell or exoskeleton? I have met many individuals who possess such things, it is nothing to be ashamed of]{Morra},” Morra reassured.

“[I’m not ashamed. It’s part of me. It protects me, what could I possibly be ashamed of?]{Zion Daybreaker}” questioned Zion. This conversation was starting to get on his nerves.

“[Well, to begin: you seem to avoid my questions in regard to your headpiece…]{Morra}” explained Morra, pointing to the halo above Zion’s head.

“[Please go away.]{Zion Daybreaker}”

# Chapter 3: Day three.

I’m not sure how much longer I can last.

Not in regard to my physical well-being. In fact, I have been nourishing fairly well, and my holodeck vital scanner says I am on track for a healthy week. Except for my total lack of sleep… that isn’t the point, though.

I’m talking about my mental well-being. I am absolutely, unequivocally, critically bored. I have watched this dead, still ocean for days, and have found absolutely nothing of note. I asked Edmin to scan under the water, and there was still nothing. I even tried to contact Seth’s ship to see what he saw from orbit, but when he answered, all I heard were feminine voices and some… crude noises in the background.

The morning report from the Llamanian Republic was embarrassing. Yet again I had to report that we’ve found nothing. The worst part, though, was that right after the commander asked if we were “even looking,” Dutch yelled over the communicators, “Yo, Zion, let’s play Resodraft!”

Needless to say, I was reprimanded greatly. The commander demanded to speak with Llawdon, but I told him he was asleep. He seemed awfully understanding after that, though, mentioning something about “growing pains.” What does that even mean? He has been out cold for days. Then again, at least he’s not nagging us with snarky comments. Now it’s just Dutch, and Edmin, and sometimes Morra doing that.

Maybe I’m really just upset about the captain’s—

“[ATTENTION: Zion. I have come to impart my status report]{Edmin},” stated Edmin, who had apparently been waiting at the cockpit.

“[Edmin, yes. You just made my day. Please tell me you have good news]{Zion Daybreaker},” Zion implored.

“[Indeed. Structural analysis has revealed that my new chassis implant has improved stability by 48.52%. Additionally, the upgraded battery will increase charge capacity by 2.63 megawatts]{Edmin},” the droid explained.

“[That’s… that’s great, Edmin. Thank you for the update]{Zion Daybreaker},” sighed Zion. He was hoping for something a little more relevant to the mission. “[Is there anything else?]{Zion Daybreaker}”

“[Your reaction does not logically compute. I have informed you of good news, yet you are disappointed. Please explain your dismay]{Edmin},” Edmin requested.

“[Just a little tired.]{Zion Daybreaker}”
